chapters.title_en: The Categories of the Deluded — Section 1: On the Delusion of the Disbeliever and the Sinner
chapters.arabic_text:
### | بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

### | مقدمة المؤلف

قال الشيخ الإمام العالم العامل حجة الإسلام أبو حامد محمد بن محمد
الغزالى الطوسى رحم الله وعفا عنه: الحمد لله وحده والصلاة والسلام على خير
خلقة سيدنا محمد وآله وصحبه، هذا كتاب الكشف والتبيين فى غرور الخلق
أجمعين. اعلم أن الخلق قسمان: حيوان وغير حيوان.. والحيوان قسمان: مكلف
ومهمل.. فالمكلف من خاطبه الله بالعبادة وأمره بها.. ووعده الثواب عليها
ونهاه عن المعاصى وحذره العقوبة..
ثم المكلف قسمان: مؤمن وكافر.. والمؤمن قسمان طائع وعاص.. وكل من
الطائعين والعاصين ينقسم قسمين: عالم وجاهل..
ثم رأيت الغرور لازما لجميع المؤمنين المكلفين والكافرين. إلا من عصمه
الله رب العالمين.. وأنا بحمد الله أكشف عن غرورهم وأبين الحجة فيه..
وأوضحه غاية الإيضاح. وأبينه غاية البيان بأوجز ما تكون العبارة.. وأبدع ما
يكون من الإشارة.
والمغرورون من الخلق ما عدا الكافرين أربعة أصناف: صنف من العلماء.. وصنف
من العباد.. وصنف من أرباب الأموال..وصنف من المتصوفة.

### | غرور الكافر

فأول ما نبدأ به غرور الكافر، وهو قسمان: منهم من غرته الحياة الدنيا..
ومنهم من غره بالله الغرور.. أما الذين غرتهم الحياة الدنيا وهم الذين
قالوا: النقد خير من النسيئة.. ولذات الدنيا يقين.. ولذات الآخرة شك!!..
ولا يترك اليقين بالشك.. وهذا قياس فاسد.. وهو قياس إبليس لعنه الله تعالى
فى قوله: أنا خير منه.. فظن أن الخيرية فى النسب..

### | وعلاج هذا الغرور شيئان

إما بتصديق وهو الإيمان.. وإما ببرهان.
أما التصديق فهو أن يصدق الله تعالى فى قوله (وما عند الله خير وأبقى)
(وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور) .. وتصديق الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
فيما جاء به..وأما البرهان: وهو أن يعرف وجه فساد قياسه.. أن قوله: الدنيا
نقد والآخرة نسيئة مقدمة صحيحة وأما قوله: النقد خير من النسيئة. فهو محل
التلبيس.. وليس الأمر
كذلك.. بل إن كان النقد مثل النسيئة في المقدار.. والمقصود فهو خير.. وإن
كان أقل منها.. فالنسيئة خير منه.. ومعلوم أن الآخرة أبدية.. والدنيا غير
أبدية.. وأما قوله: ولذات  الدنيا يقين ولذات الآخرة شك فهو أيضا باطل.. بل
ذلك يقين عند المؤمنين..
وليقينه مدر كان: أحدهما الإيمان والتصديق على وجه التقليد للأنبياء
والعلماء كما يقلد الطبيب الحاذق في الدواء.. والمدرك الثاني: الوحى
للأنبياء والإلهام للأولياء.. ولا تظن أن معرفة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
لأمور الآخرة.. ولأمور الدنيا تقليد لجبريل عليه السلام.. فإن التقليد ليس
بمعرفة صحيحة.. والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حاشاه الله من ذلك.. بل انكشفت
له الأشياء.. وشاهدها بنور البصيرة.. كما شاهدت أنت المحسوسات بالعين
الظاهرة..

### | فصل فيمن يشاركون الكفار غرورهم

### | من المؤمنين بربهم

والمؤمنون بألسنتهم وعقائدهم إذا ضيعوا أمر الله تعالى وهى الأعمال
الصالحة.. وتدنسوا بالشهوات.. وهم مشاركون الكفار فى هذا الغرور.. فالحياة
الدنيا للكافرين والمؤمنين جميعا غرور: فأما غرور الكافرين بالله تعالى
فمثاله:
قول بعضهم فى أنفسهم بألسنتهم: إنه إن كان الله معيدنا فنحن أحق بها من
غيرنا كما أخبر الله تعالى عنهم فى صورة الكهف حين قال: (ما أظن أن تبيد
هذه أبدا، وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربي لأجدن خيرا منها منقلبا)

### | ما سبب هذا الغرور

وسبب هذا الغرور قياس من أقيسة إبليس لعنه الله تعالى.. وذلك انهم ينظرون
مرة إلى نعم الله تعالى عليهم في الدنيا.. فيقيسون عليها نعم الآخرة، ومرة
ينظرون إلى تأخير عذاب الله عنهم في الدنيا فيقيسون عذاب الآخرة كما أخبر
الله تعالى عنهم (ويقولون فى أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله بما نقول حسبهم جهنم
يصلونها فبئس المصير) ومرة ينظرون إلى المؤمنين وهم فقراء.. فيزدرونهم
ويقولون: (أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا) .. ويقولون: (لو كان خيرا ما
سبقونا إليه) ..
وترتيب القياس الذى نظم فى قلوبهم أنهم يقولون: قد أحسن الله إلينا بنعم
الدنيا.. وكل محسن فهو محب، وكل محب فهو محسن، وليس كذلك.. بل يكون محسنا
ولا يكون محبا.. بل ربما يكون الإحسان سبب هلاكه على الاستدراج.. وذلك محض
الغرور بالله عز
وجل.. ولذلك قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: (إن الله تعالى يحمى عبده من
الدنيا  كما يحمى أحدكم مريضه عن الطعام والشراب وهو يحبه) .. ولذلك كان
أرباب البصائر إذا أقبلت عليهم الدنيا حزنوا، وإذا أقبل عليهم الفقر
فرحوا.. وقالوا: مرحبا بشعار الصالحين، فقد قال الله تعالى: (فأما الإنسان
إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه) ..وقال تعالى: (أيحسبون أنما نمدهم به من
مال وبنين نسارع لهم فى الخيرات بل لا يشعرون) .. الآية.. وقال تعالى:
(سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون، وأملى لهم إن كيدى متين) .. وقال تعالى:
(فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شئ حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا
أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون) ..
فمن آمن بالله تعالى يأمن من هذا الغرور..

### | ومم ينشأ هذا الغرور

ومنشأ هذا الغرور الجهل بالله تعالى.. وبصفاته.. فإن من عرف الله تعالى
فلا يأمن من مكر الله.. وينظرون إلى فرعون وهامان وثمود وماذا حل بهم.. مع
أن الله تعالى أعطاهم من المال.. وقد حذر الله
تعالى مكره فقال تعالى: (فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون) .. وقال
تعالى: (ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين) .. وقال تعالى: (فمهل
الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا) .. فمن أولى نعمة يحذر أن تكون نقمة.

### | فصل فى غرور عصاة المؤمنين

### | وهم من يتكلون على عفو الله ويهملون العمل

وأما غرور العصاة بالله من المؤمنين فقولهم: غفور رحيم، وإنما يرجى عفوه
فاتكلوا على ذلك وأهملوا الأعمال وذلك من قبل الرجا فإنه مقام محمود في
الدنيا. وأن رحمة الله واسعة ونعمته وشاملة وكرمه عميم، وأنا موحدون نرجوه
بوسيلة الإيمان والكرم والإحسان.

### | منشأ ذاك الغرور

وربما كان منشأ حالهم التمسك بصلاح الآباء والأمهات.. وذلك نهاية الغرور
فإن آباءهم مع صلاحهم وورعهم كانوا خائفين.. ونظم قياسهم الذى سول لهم
الشيطان: من أحب إنسانا أحب أولاده.. فإن الله قد أحب أباكم فهو يحبكم فلا
تحتاجون إلى الطاعات، فاتكلوا على ذلك واغتروا بالله، ولم يعلموا أن نوحا
عليه
السلام، أراد أن يحمل ولده فى السفينة فمنع، وأغرقه إليه سبحانه وتعالى
بأشد ما أغرق به قوم نوح..
وإن نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه  وسلم استأذن فى زيارة قبر أمه.. وفى
الاستغفار: فأذن له فى الزيارة ولم يؤذن فى الاستغفار لها..
ونسوا قوله سبحانه وتعلى: (ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى. وأن ليس للإنسان إلا
ما سعى) ..
ومن ظن أنه ينجو بتقوى أصله كمن ظن أنه يشبع بأكل أبيه أو يروى بشراب
أبيه..
والتقوى فرض عين لا يجزى فيها والد عن ولده (يوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه
وأبيه وصاحبته وبنيه) .. إلا على سبيل الشفاعة..
ونسوا قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام: (الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل لما بعد الموت،
والأحمق من أتبع نفسه وهواها وتمنى على الله الأماني) .
وقوله تعالى: (إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا وجاهدوا فى سبيل الله أولئك
يرجون رحمة الله والله غفور رحيم) .
وقال تعالى: (جزاء بما كانوا يعملون) .. وهل يصح الرجا إلا إذا تقدمه عمل
وإلا فهو غرور لا محالة..
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "heedlessness" and being deceived by that which appears beneficial but conceals harm; al-ghirrah is the state of one who is unmindful of consequences.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, al-ghurūr is the soul's reliance upon a false semblance of security, often against God's warnings — a cognitive and moral failure rooted in ignorance of God's attributes.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "to be deceived by a mirage or by one who flatters." Metaphorically (majāz), it denotes the soul's being beguiled by worldly goods or by false hopes of divine indulgence without merit.
- Root: ق-ي-س (q-y-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To measure, compare, or analogize; the act of drawing an inference from one case to another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyās in kalām is the rational method of analogical reasoning; its validity depends on the soundness of the shared attribute (ʿillah). A corrupt qiyās is the root of theological error.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: measuring a garment with a measure. Metaphorical: applying a judgment of one thing to another based on assumed similarity — here, the false analogy of the disbelievers.
- Root: ر-ج-و (r-j-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To hope, expect, or desire something anticipated; the opposite of despair (ya's).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Rajā' is a praiseworthy station (maqām maḥmūd) when accompanied by fear (khawf) and action; without action, it degenerates into mere wishful thinking (tamannī) and delusion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: hoping for rain. Metaphorical: the soul's expectation of divine mercy — valid only when preceded by sincere endeavor.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditionality in Nominal Sentences (al-sharṭ fī al-jumlah al-ismiyyah) — The syntactic structure "إن كان النقد مثل النسيئة... فهو خير" establishes a conditional relation where the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is governed by the protasis (sharṭ), demonstrating that the disbelievers' categorical claim ("the present is better than the deferred") is logically unsound because it omits the necessary condition of equality in quantity and purpose.
chapters.translation:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

The Author's Introduction

The Shaykh, the Imām, the learned and the practicing, the Proof of Islam, Abū Ḥāmid Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Ghazālī al-Ṭūsī — may God have mercy upon him and pardon him — said: Praise be to God alone, and blessings and peace upon the best of His creation, our master Muḥammad, and upon his family and companions. This is the book of Unveiling and Clarification concerning the delusion of all creation.

Know that creation is of two kinds: animate and inanimate. The animate is of two kinds: the obligated (mukallaf) and the neglected. The obligated is he whom God addressed with worship and commanded it, promised reward for it, forbade him from sins, and warned him of punishment.

Then the obligated is of two kinds: believer and disbeliever. The believer is of two kinds: obedient and disobedient. And each of the obedient and the disobedient is divided into two kinds: learned and ignorant.

Then I saw that delusion (ghurūr) is inseparable from all obligated believers and disbelievers — except those whom God, Lord of the worlds, has protected. And I, by God's praise, shall unveil their delusion and clarify the proof concerning it, and elucidate it to the utmost clarity, and explain it with the utmost exposition, in the most concise expression and the most exquisite allusion.

The deluded among creation, apart from the disbelievers, are four classes: a class of the scholars, a class of the worshippers, a class of the wealthy, and a class of the Sufis.

On the Delusion of the Disbeliever

The first thing we begin with is the delusion of the disbeliever, and it is of two kinds: among them is he whom the life of this world deluded, and among them is he whom "the Deluder" deluded concerning God. As for those whom the life of this world deluded — and they are those who said: "The ready cash is better than the credit; the pleasures of this world are certain, and the pleasures of the Hereafter are doubtful; and one does not abandon certainty for doubt." This is a corrupt analogy (qiyās fāsid), and it is the analogy of Iblīs — may God curse him — in his saying: "I am better than him," for he supposed that superiority lay in lineage.

The Remedy for This Delusion Is Two Things

Either by affirmation (taṣdīq), which is faith, or by demonstration (burhān).

As for affirmation, it is that one affirms the truth of God — exalted — in His saying: {«وما عند الله خير وأبقى»} ("What is with God is better and more enduring") and {«وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور»} ("And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion"), and affirms the truth of the Messenger — peace be upon him — in what he brought.

As for the demonstration, it is that one recognizes the aspect of corruption in his analogy. For his saying "the world is ready cash and the Hereafter is credit" is a sound premise. But his saying "the ready cash is better than the credit" — that is the locus of obfuscation (talbīs). The matter is not so. Rather, if the ready cash equals the credit in quantity and purpose, then it is better. But if it is less than it, then the credit is better than it. And it is known that the Hereafter is eternal, and the world is not eternal.

As for his saying "the pleasures of this world are certain and the pleasures of the Hereafter are doubtful" — this too is false. Rather, that is certain for the believers. And for this certainty there are two means of apprehension: one is faith and affirmation by way of emulation (taqlīd) of the prophets and the scholars, just as one emulates the skilled physician concerning medicine. The second means of apprehension is revelation (waḥy) for the prophets and inspiration (ilhām) for the saints. And do not suppose that the Prophet's — peace be upon him — knowledge of the matters of the Hereafter and the matters of this world was emulation of Gabriel — peace be upon him. For emulation is not sound knowledge, and the Prophet — peace be upon him — God forbid that — rather, things were unveiled to him, and he witnessed them with the light of inner vision (nūr al-baṣīrah), just as you witness sensible objects with the outer eye.

Section: On Those Among the Believers in Their Lord Who Share the Delusion of the Disbelievers

And those who believe with their tongues and their creeds — when they neglect the command of God — exalted — which is the righteous deeds, and defile themselves with lusts — they share with the disbelievers in this delusion. For the life of this world is a delusion for both disbelievers and believers alike.

As for the delusion of the disbelievers concerning God — exalted — its example is the saying of some of them among themselves, with their tongues: "If God is to return us, then we are more deserving of it than others" — as God — exalted — reported of them in Sūrat al-Kahf when He said: {«ما أظن أن تبيد هذه أبدا، وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رددت إلى ربي لأجدن خيرا منها منقلبا»} ("I do not think that this will ever perish, and I do not think the Hour will come, and if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a return").

What Is the Cause of This Delusion

The cause of this delusion is an analogy from the analogies of Iblīs — may God curse him. For they look, at one time, at God's blessings upon them in this world, and they analogize upon them the blessings of the Hereafter. And at another time, they look at the deferment of God's punishment from them in this world, and they analogize the punishment of the Hereafter — as God — exalted — reported of them: {«ويقولون فى أنفسهم لولا يعذبنا الله بما نقول حسبهم جهنم يصلونها فبئس المصير»} ("And they say among themselves: 'Why does God not punish us for what we say?' Sufficient for them is Hell; they will burn in it, and evil is the destination"). And at another time, they look at the believers who are poor, and they despise them and say: {«أهؤلاء من الله عليهم من بيننا»} ("Are these the ones whom God has favored among us?") and they say: {«لو كان خيرا ما سبقونا إليه»} ("If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it").

The arrangement of the analogy that was organized in their hearts is that they say: "God has been good to us with the blessings of this world, and every doer of good is a lover, and every lover is a doer of good." But it is not so. Rather, one may be a doer of good without being a lover. Indeed, sometimes the good deed is the cause of one's destruction by way of gradual enticement (istidrāj). And that is pure delusion concerning God — mighty and majestic. For this reason, the Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "God — exalted — protects His servant from this world just as one of you protects his sick patient from food and drink, while He loves him." For this reason, the people of inner vision (arbāb al-baṣā'ir), when this world advanced upon them, grieved; and when poverty advanced upon them, they rejoiced and said: "Welcome to the emblem of the righteous." For God — exalted — has said: {«فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه»} ("As for man, when his Lord tests him and honors him and favors him...") and He — exalted — said: {«أيحسبون أنما نمدهم به من مال وبنين نسارع لهم فى الخيرات بل لا يشعرون»} ("Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children — that We hasten for them good things? Rather, they do not perceive") — the verse. And He — exalted — said: {«سنستدرجهم من حيث لا يعلمون، وأملى لهم إن كيدى متين»} ("We will gradually entice them from where they do not know, and I will respite them; indeed, My plan is firm"). And He — exalted — said: {«فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شئ حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون»} ("And when they forgot what they were reminded of, We opened upon them the doors of everything, until when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and behold, they were in despair").

So whoever believes in God — exalted — is secure from this delusion.

From What Does This Delusion Arise

The origin of this delusion is ignorance of God — exalted — and of His attributes. For whoever knows God — exalted — is not secure from God's stratagem (makr). And they should look at Pharaoh, Hāmān, and Thamūd, and what befell them — despite the fact that God — exalted — had given them wealth. And God — exalted — has warned against His stratagem, saying: {«فلا يأمن مكر الله إلا القوم الخاسرون»} ("None is secure from God's stratagem except the people of loss"), and He — exalted — said: {«ومكروا ومكر الله والله خير الماكرين»} ("And they plotted, and God plotted, and God is the best of plotters"), and He — exalted — said: {«فمهل الكافرين أمهلهم رويدا»} ("So give respite to the disbelievers; grant them respite gently"). So whoever is given a blessing should fear that it may be a punishment.

Section: On the Delusion of the Disobedient Among the Believers

And they are those who rely upon God's pardon and neglect action.

As for the delusion of the disobedient among the believers concerning God, it is their saying: "He is Forgiving, Merciful, and His pardon is to be hoped for." So they relied upon that and neglected the deeds. This arises from hope (rajā'), for it is a praiseworthy station in this world, and that God's mercy is vast, His favor comprehensive, and His generosity abundant — and we are monotheists, hoping in Him through the means of faith, generosity, and beneficence.

The Origin of That Delusion

Perhaps the origin of their state is their clinging to the righteousness of their fathers and mothers. And that is the extreme of delusion. For their fathers, despite their righteousness and piety, were fearful. And the arrangement of their analogy, which Satan embellished for them, is: "Whoever loves a person loves his children. God has loved your father, so He loves you. Therefore you have no need of acts of obedience." So they relied upon that and were deluded concerning God. And they did not know that Noah — peace be upon him — wanted to carry his son upon the ark and was prevented, and God — glorified and exalted — drowned him with the most severe drowning with which He drowned the people of Noah.

And our Prophet Muḥammad — peace be upon him — sought permission to visit his mother's grave and to seek forgiveness for her. He was granted permission for the visit but was not granted permission to seek forgiveness for her.

And they forgot His saying — glorified and exalted: {«ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى. وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى»} ("That no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another, and that man has nothing but what he strives for").

And whoever supposes that he will be saved by the piety of his origin is like one who supposes he will be satiated by his father's eating or quenched by his father's drinking. And piety is an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn); no parent suffices for his child in it — {«يوم يفر المرء من أخيه وأمه وأبيه وصاحبته وبنيه»} ("On the day when a man flees from his brother, his mother, his father, his spouse, and his sons") — except by way of intercession.

And they forgot his saying — peace and blessings be upon him: "The shrewd one is he who takes account of himself and works for what is after death, and the foolish one is he who follows his soul and its desires and wishes upon God wishes (tamannī)."

And His saying — exalted: {«إن الذين آمنوا والذين هاجروا وجاهدوا فى سبيل الله أولئك يرجون رحمة الله والله غفور رحيم»} ("Indeed, those who believed and those who emigrated and strove in the path of God — those hope for the mercy of God, and God is Forgiving, Merciful").

And He — exalted — said: {«جزاء بما كانوا يعملون»} ("A recompense for what they used to do"). And does hope (rajā') become sound except when action precedes it? Otherwise, it is delusion, inevitably.

chapters.title_en: Section 2 — On the Delusion of Those Who Trust in Their Few Good Deeds Despite Abundant Sins, and the Categories of the Deluded Among the Scholars
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فصل فيمن اغتر بحسناته مع قلتها وكثرة سيئاته

ويقرب منهم غرور طوائف لهم طاعات ومعاص إلا أن معاصيهم أكثر وهم يتوقعون
المغفرة ويظنون أن لغة حسناتهم ترجح أكثر من كفة السيئات.. وهذا غاية
الجهل، فيرى الواحد يتصرف بدراهم معدودة من الحلال والحرام ويكون ما تناوله
من أموال الناس والشبهات أضعافا وهو كمن وضع فى كفة الميزان عشرة دراهم
ووضع فى الكفة الأخرى ألفا وأراد أن تميل الكفة التى فيها العشرة وذلك غاية
الجهل..

### | فصل فى غرور من يظن أن طاعته أكثر من معاصيه

وإذا عمل طاعة حفظها واعتد بها كالذى يستغفر بلسانه أو يسبح فى الليل
والنهار مثلا مائة مرة أو ألف مرة ثم يغتاب المسلمين وتكلم بما لا يرضاه
الله طول النهار، ويلتفت إلى ما ورد فى فضل التسبيح.. ويغفل عما ورد فى
عقوبة المغتابين والكذابين والنمامين والمنافقين.. وذلك محض الغرور فحفظ
لسانه عن المعاصى آكد من تسبيحاته.

### | فصل فى بيان المغرورين وأقسام كل صنف

### | الصنف الأول

### | من المغرورين العلماء

والمغرورون منهم فرق:

### | الفرقة الأولى

فرقة منهم لما أحكمت العلوم الشرعية والعقلية تعمقوا فيها واشتغلوا بها
وأهملوا تفقد الجوارح وحفظها عن  المعاصى، وإلزامها الطاعات فاغتروا بعلمهم
وظنوا أنهم عند الله بمكان.. وأنهم قد بلغوا من العلم مبلغا لا يعذب الله
تعالى مثلهم، بل يقبل عليهم ويقبل فى الخلق شفاعتهم، ولا يطالبهم بذنوبهم،
وخطاياهم وهو مغرورون فإنهم لو نظروا بعين البصيرة علموا أن العلم علمان:
(1) علم معاملة.
(2) وعلم مكاشفة.
وعلم المكاشفة وهو العلم بالله تعالى وبصفاته.. ولا بد من علم المعاملة
لتتم الحكمة المقصودة وهى العلم بمعرفة الحلال الحرام ومعرفة أخلاق الناس
المذمومة والمحمودة..
ومثالهم مثال طبيب طب غيره وهو عليل قادر على طب نفسه ولم يفعل.. وهل
ينفع الدواء بالوصف؟!.. هيهات لا ينفع الدواء إلا من شربه بعد الحمية..
وغفلوا عن قوله سبحانه وتعالى: (قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دسها) ولم يقل
من يعلم تزكيتها وأهمل علمها وعلمها الناس..
وغفلوا عن قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (إن أشد الناس عذابا يوم القيامة
عالم لم ينفعه الله بعلمه) .
وغير ذلك كثير..
وهؤلاء المغرورن - نعوذ بالله منهم - وإنما غلب عليهم حب الدنيا وحب
الآخرة وحب الراحة.. وظنوا أن علمهم ينحيهم فى الآخرة من غير عمل.

### | الفرقة الثانية

وفرقة أخرى أحكموا العلم والعمل الظاهر وتركوا المعاصى الظاهرة وغفلوا عن
قلوبهم فلم يمحو منها الصفات المذمومة عند الله كالكبر والرياء والحسد وطلب
الرياسة والعلا وإرادة الثناء على الأقران والشركاء وطلب الشهرة فى البلاد
والعباد، وذلك غرور
سببه غفلتهم عن قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام: (الرياء الشرك الأصغر) .
وقوله: (الحسد يأكل الحسنات كما تأكل النار الحطب) .
وقوله: (حب المال والشرف ينبتان النفاق في القلب كما ينبت الماء البقل) .
إلى غير ذلك من الأخبار.. وغفلوا عن قوله تعالى: (إلا من أتى الله بقلب
سليم) .
فغفلوا عن قلوبهم واشتغلوا بظواهرهم.. ومن لا يصفى قلبه لا تصح طاعته..
ويكون كمريض ظهر به الجرب فأمره الطبيب بالطلاء وشرب الدواء.. فاشتغل
بالطلاء وترك شرب الدواء.. فأزال ما بظاهره.. ولم يزل ما بباطنه.. وأصل ما
على ظاهره مما فى باطنه.. فلا يزال جربه يزداد أبدا مما فى باطنه..
فكذلك الخبائث إذا  كانت كامنة فى القلب يظهر أثرها على الجوارح، فلو زال
ما فى باطنه استراح الظاهر.

### | الفرقة الثالثة

وفرقة أخرى علموا هذه الأخلاق.. وعلموا أنها مذمومة من وجه الشرع إلا
أنهم لعجبهم بأنفسهم يظنون أنهم منفكون.. وأنهم أرفع
عند الله من أن يبتليهم بذلك.. وإنما يبتلى به العوام دون من بلغ مبلغهم
فى العلم.. فأما هم فإنهم أعظم عند الله من أن يبتليهم.. فظهرت عليهم مخايل
الكبر والرياسة.. وطلبوا العلو والشرف.. وغرورهم أنهم ظنوا ذلك ليس تكبرا..
وإنما هو عز الدين، وإظهار لشرف العلم.. ونصرة الدين.. وغفلوا عن فرح إبليس
به.. ونصرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لماذا كانت؟.. وبماذا أرغم الكافرين؟
وغفلوا عن تواضع الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم أجمعين.. وتذللهم وفقرهم
ومسكنتهم حتى عوتب عمر رضى الله عنه فى بذاذته عند قدومه إلى الشام فقال:
إنا قوم عزنا الله بالإسلام.. ولا نطلب العزة فى غيره..
ثم هذا المغرور يطلب العز للدين بالثياب الرفيعة.. ويزعم أنه يطلب عز
الدين وشرفه.. ومهما أطلق اللسان فى الحسد فى أقرانه أو فيمن رد عليه شيئا
من كلامه لم يظن بنفسه أن ذلك حسد.. ويقول: إنما هو غضب للحق ورد على
المبطل فى عدوانه وظلمه.. وهذ مغرور.. فإنه لو طعن في غيره من العلماء من
أقرانه ربما لم يغضب، بل ربما يفرح - وإن أظهر الغضب عند الناس بأنه يحبه..
وربما يظهر العلم ويقول: غرضى به أن أفيد الخلق.. وهو هراء لأنه لو كان
غرضه صلاح الخلق لأحب صلاحهم على يد غيره ممن هو مثله أو فوقه.
وربما يدخل على السلطان ويتودد إليه ويثنى عليه.. فإذا سئل عن
ذلك قال: إنما غرضى أن أنفع المسلمين.. وأن أرفع عنهم الضرر.. وهو مغرور.
ولو كان غرضه ذلك فرح به إذا جرى على يد غيره ولو رأى من هو مثله عند
السلطان يشفع فى أحد يغضب.. وربما أخذ من أموالهم فإن خطر بباله أنه حرام
قال له الشيطان هذا مال لا مالك له وهو لمصالح المسلمين وأنت إمام المسلمين
وعالمهم وبك قوام الدين.. وهذه ثلاثة تلبيسات.
أحدها: أنه مال لا مالك له.
والثانى: أنه لمصالح المسلمين.
والثالث: أنه إمام..
وهل يكون إماما إلا من أعرض عن الدنيا كالأنبياء والصحابة..
ومثله: قول عيسى عليه السلام: العالم السوء كصخرة وقعت فى الوادى فلا هى
تشرب الماء ولا هى تترك الماء يخلص إلى الزرع..
وأصناف غرور أهل العلم كثيرة.. وما يفسد هؤلاء أكثر مما يصلحونه..

### | الفرقة الرابعة

وفرقة أخرى حكموا العلم.. وطهروا الجوارح وزينوها بالطاعات.. واجتنبوا
ظاهر المعاصى.. وتفقدوا أخلاق النفس وصفات القلب من الرياء.. والحسد والكبر
والحقد.. وطلب
العلو.. وجاهدوا أنفسكم فى التبرى منها وقلعوا من القلب منابتها الجلية
القوية.. ولكنهم مغرورون إذ بقى فى زوايا القلب بقايا من خفايا مكايد
الشيطان.. خبايا خدع النفس ما دق وغمض.. فلم يفطنوا لها.. وأهملوها..
ومثالهم كمثل من يريد تنقية الزرع من الحشيش فدار عليه.. وفتش عن كل حشيش
فقلعه.. إلا أنه لم يفتش عما لم يخرج رأسه بعد من تحت الأرض وظن أن الكل قد
ظهر وبرز فلما غفل عنها ظهرت وأفسدت عليه الزرع. وهؤلاء إن غيروا تغيروا..
وربما تركوا مخالطة الخلق استكبارا.. وربما نظروا إليهم بعين الحقارة..
وربما يجتهد بعضهم فى تحسين نظمه لئلا ينظر إليه بعين الركاكة..

- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "heedlessness" and "being deceived by appearances"; al-ghirrah is the state of one who is unmindful of consequences, akin to one asleep or a young bird easily caught.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, al-ghurūr is the soul's false reliance on something that will not avail it in the Hereafter—such as trusting in mere knowledge or ritual without purifying the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for "deception" (khidāʿ) and metaphorically for the soul's self-flattery (iʿjāb bi-l-nafs); the deluded one (maghrūr) is one who builds on a mirage.
- Root: ك-ف-ء (k-f-') [Note: Root ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) is used for "sufficiency"; here the anchor is on the balance metaphor]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Al-kaffah is the pan of a scale; the verb kafā means "to suffice" or "to be enough."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The balance (mīzān) is a Quranic metaphor for divine justice in weighing deeds; the weight (tarjīḥ) of good deeds over evil ones is determined by sincerity and conformity to the Law, not by quantity alone.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical weighing; metaphorical for the moral reckoning where the heavier pan indicates preponderance of merit.
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "knowledge" or "perception" of a thing as it is; ʿilm is the firm comprehension of reality.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, ʿilm is divided into ʿilm al-muʿāmalah (knowledge of practical religion—what to do and avoid) and ʿilm al-mukāshafah (knowledge of unveiling—direct apprehension of God and His attributes). The former is a means; the latter is the end.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for acquired knowledge; metaphorically, the "scholar" (ʿālim) who does not act is like a tree that bears no fruit—knowledge is a proof against him, not for him.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīm wa Taʾkhīr (Fronting and Delaying) — In the sentence "قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دسها" (He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it), the verb is fronted to indicate exclusivity and emphasis (ḥaṣr), showing that success is contingent solely on purification, not on mere knowledge of it.
chapters.translation:
### Section on the Delusion of Those Who Trust in Their Few Good Deeds Despite the Abundance of Their Sins

Near to them [in delusion] are groups who have acts of obedience and acts of disobedience, except that their disobediences are more numerous, yet they expect forgiveness and suppose that the "language" of their good deeds will outweigh the pan of their evil deeds. This is the extreme of ignorance. For one of them sees himself transacting with a few counted dirhams—some lawful, some unlawful—while what he consumes of people's wealth and of ambiguous matters is manifold. He is like one who places ten dirhams in one pan of the balance and a thousand in the other, then desires that the pan containing the ten should tip the scale. That is the extreme of ignorance.

### Section on the Delusion of One Who Thinks His Obedience Exceeds His Disobediences

When he performs an act of obedience, he preserves it and counts it—like one who seeks forgiveness with his tongue, or glorifies [God] night and day, for example, a hundred times or a thousand times—then he backbites the Muslims and speaks all day long of what God does not approve. He pays heed to what has been reported concerning the virtue of glorification, but is heedless of what has been reported concerning the punishment of backbiters, liars, slanderers, and hypocrites. That is pure delusion. For guarding one's tongue from disobediences is more incumbent than one's glorifications.

### Section Explaining the Deluded and the Categories of Each Class

### The First Class: The Scholars Among the Deluded

The deluded among them are of several groups:

### The First Group

A group among them, when they mastered the religious and rational sciences, delved deeply into them and occupied themselves with them, but neglected the examination of their bodily members, guarding them from disobediences, and compelling them to acts of obedience. So they were deluded by their knowledge and supposed that they hold a station with God—that they have reached such a degree of knowledge that God will not punish the like of them, but rather will turn to them and accept their intercession for creation, and will not call them to account for their sins and errors. They are deluded. For had they looked with the eye of insight, they would know that knowledge is of two kinds: (1) knowledge of practical dealing (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah), and (2) knowledge of unveiling (ʿilm al-mukāshafah). Knowledge of unveiling is knowledge of God Most High and His attributes. But knowledge of practical dealing is indispensable to complete the intended wisdom—namely, knowledge of the lawful and the unlawful, and knowledge of people's blameworthy and praiseworthy traits.

Their example is the example of a physician who treats others while he himself is ill, capable of treating himself, yet does not do so. Does the medicine benefit by mere description? Far from it! The medicine benefits only the one who drinks it after abstaining [from what harms]. They were heedless of His saying, Most High: {«قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دسها»} ("He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it")—and He did not say "who knows its purification" while neglecting its practice and teaching it to people.

And they were heedless of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Verily, the most severely punished of people on the Day of Resurrection is a scholar whom God did not benefit with his knowledge."

And much else besides. These are the deluded—we seek refuge in God from them. What overcame them was love of this world, love of the Hereafter, and love of ease. They supposed that their knowledge would set them apart in the Hereafter without any work.

### The Second Group

Another group mastered knowledge and outward works, abandoned outward disobediences, but were heedless of their hearts—they did not erase from them the traits blameworthy to God, such as pride, ostentation (riyāʾ), envy, seeking leadership and elevation, desiring praise from peers and partners, and seeking fame in the lands and among people. That is delusion, caused by their heedlessness of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Ostentation is the lesser shirk." And his saying: "Envy consumes good deeds as fire consumes wood." And his saying: "Love of wealth and honor sprouts hypocrisy in the heart as water sprouts vegetation." And other reports besides. And they were heedless of His saying, Most High: {«إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم»} ("Except him who comes to God with a sound heart").

So they were heedless of their hearts and occupied themselves with their outward forms. Whoever does not purify his heart, his obedience is not sound. He is like a sick man afflicted with scabies on his skin; the physician ordered him to apply ointment and drink medicine. He occupied himself with the ointment and neglected drinking the medicine. So he removed what was on his exterior but did not remove what was in his interior—and the origin of what is on his exterior is from what is in his interior. Thus his scabies keeps increasing forever from what is within him. Likewise, when impurities are latent in the heart, their effect appears on the bodily members. Were what is in the interior removed, the exterior would find rest.

### The Third Group

Another group knew these traits and knew they are blameworthy from the standpoint of the Law—except that, due to their self-admiration, they suppose they are free of them, and that they are loftier with God than to be tried by them. They think such trials afflict only the common folk, not those who have reached their degree of knowledge. As for them, they are too great with God to be tried. So the signs of pride and love of leadership appeared on them, and they sought elevation and honor. Their delusion is that they supposed this is not pride, but rather the might of religion, the manifestation of the honor of knowledge, and the defense of the faith. They were heedless of Iblīs's joy at this. And for what purpose was the Prophet's—peace and blessings be upon him—victory? And by what did he subdue the disbelievers? They were heedless of the humility of the Companions—may God be pleased with them all—their lowliness, their poverty, and their meekness, until ʿUmar—may God be pleased with him—was reproached for his shabbiness upon his arrival in Syria, and he said: "We are a people whom God has honored with Islam, and we seek no honor in anything else."

Then this deluded one seeks honor for religion through fine garments, claiming he seeks the might and honor of religion. And whenever he unleashes his tongue in envy against his peers, or against one who refutes something of his speech, he does not suppose of himself that this is envy. He says: "It is only anger for the truth and rebuttal of the wrongdoer in his transgression and injustice." This one is deluded. For were another scholar among his peers to be attacked, perhaps he would not be angered—rather, he might even rejoice, though he displays anger before people, claiming he loves him. And perhaps he displays knowledge and says: "My aim in this is to benefit creation." This is nonsense. For were his aim the betterment of creation, he would love their betterment at the hands of another like him or above him.

And perhaps he enters upon the Sultan, ingratiates himself, and praises him. When asked about that, he says: "My aim is only to benefit the Muslims and to ward off harm from them." He is deluded. Were that his aim, he would rejoice if it were accomplished at the hands of another. But if he saw someone like himself with the Sultan interceding for someone, he would be angered. And perhaps he takes from their wealth; if it occurs to his mind that it is unlawful, Satan says to him: "This is wealth with no owner; it is for the interests of the Muslims, and you are the Imām of the Muslims and their scholar, and by you the religion stands." These are three deceptions: one, that it is wealth with no owner; two, that it is for the interests of the Muslims; three, that he is the Imām. But is one an Imām except one who turns away from this world, like the Prophets and the Companions?

Similar to this is the saying of Jesus—peace be upon him: "The evil scholar is like a rock that fell into a valley: it neither drinks the water nor lets the water reach the crops."

The categories of the delusion of the people of knowledge are many. What these corrupt is more than what they set right.

### The Fourth Group

Another group mastered knowledge, purified their bodily members, adorned them with acts of obedience, avoided outward disobediences, and examined the traits of the soul and the attributes of the heart—such as ostentation, envy, pride, rancor, and seeking elevation. They strove against themselves to be free of these, and they uprooted from the heart their manifest and strong roots. But they are deluded, for there remained in the corners of the heart remnants of the hidden wiles of Satan—concealed deceptions of the soul, subtle and obscure—which they did not perceive, and so neglected. Their example is like one who wishes to cleanse a crop of weeds: he circled around it, searched for every weed, and uprooted it—except that he did not search for what had not yet emerged from beneath the earth, supposing that everything had appeared and become visible. When he was heedless of them, they emerged and ruined his crop. These, if they change, are changed. Perhaps some of them abandon mixing with people out of pride. Perhaps some look at others with an eye of contempt. Perhaps some exert themselves in refining their speech so that no one looks at them with an eye of deficiency.
